moat_against: ROIC proxy only ~5-8% in clean years and negative in FY25 (impairments) — returns sit near/below cost of capital on an acquisition-heavy capital base
Hostess deal destroyer: ~$2.9B of goodwill/trademark impairments FY25-Q3 FY26 on the $5.6B Sweet Baked Snacks acquisition; segment sales and volumes still falling (Q1 FY27 -7%)

Commodity hostage: coffee input costs drove GAAP gross margin to 33.5% in FY26 (adjusted 34.9% vs 38.2% FY25); pricing is cost-recovery, not expansion, and volumes fall when price rises (Q4 FY26 volume/mix -4pp)

Mature/declining center-store categories, private-label and retailer power, health/GLP-1 headwinds for sweet snacks and sugary spreads; net debt $6,905.1M (8.78x normalized OE, 6.1x latest-FY OE) limits flexibility
moat_for: Leading branded shelf positions: Folgers/Dunkin'/Cafe Bustelo in U.S. retail coffee, Jif peanut butter, Uncrustables (>$1B sales platform, still growing high-single-digits), Meow Mix/Milk-Bone in pet

Proven pricing power — coffee net price realization +21pp in Q4 FY26 and +13% coffee sales in Q1 FY27, taken to recover commodity costs without share collapse (~two-thirds of portfolio holding/gaining share)
Recurring, staple demand through cycles: OE positive 5/5 last years, OCF $1.2-1.5B/yr, 25 years of consecutive dividend increases
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow brand moat: leading shelf positions (Folgers/Dunkin'/Cafe Bustelo coffee, Jif, Uncrustables, Meow Mix/Milk-Bone) with proven price realization (coffee net price +21pp in Q4 FY26), but the measured economics are mid-single-digit — ROIC proxy ran only ~5-8% in clean years (FY17-22, FY24) and was negative/near-zero in the impairment years, GAAP gross margin swung 32.8%-38.8% over the last five fiscal years on coffee commodity costs and derivative marks, categories are mature with falling volumes (Q4 FY26 volume/mix -4pp), and the Hostess/Sweet Baked Snacks acquisition has absorbed ~$2.9B of impairments since FY25 — brands that earn ~6% on a goodwill-heavy capital base do not clear the 7+ moat bar.
name: The J. M. Smucker Company
one_liner: Staple-brand cash generator with a busted Hostess acquisition, moat 5/10 — on the scored median base OE $7.36/share the weighted IRR is 9.11% (IV@15% $66.30 vs $127.43), and even the tariff-flattered TTM base only reaches 15.40% / $131.61; it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$66 on the scored base.

shares_override.reason: DATA_GAP:shares - diluted shares missing for FY2024/2025/2026 in companyfacts; only a non-diluted count is filed there. The filer's own FY2026 diluted weighted-average count (106.9M) fills the gap; the engine applies this single value to every missing period. It is within 1% of each year's filed outstanding count and of the quarterly diluted counts printed through FY27 Q1 (106.9M Q4 FY26, 107.1M Q1 FY27), so the per-share distortion versus year-specific diluted counts is immaterial. Note the GAAP diluted count in the FY2025/FY2026 loss years equals basic because stock awards were anti-dilutive (release note C); the treasury-method diluted count is the economically correct denominator and is the higher, more conservative one.
shares_override.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended April 30, 2026 (filed 2026-06-09), EPS note and the FY26 results non-GAAP reconciliation (Ex. 99.1, 2026-06-09): 'Weighted-average shares outstanding - assuming dilution' 106.9M for FY2026 (FY2025: 106.6M), computed under the treasury stock method. EDGAR companyfacts carries only the non-diluted CommonStockSharesOutstanding count for FY2024-2026 (106,194,281 / 106,425,081 / 106,661,858), which is the DATA_GAP:shares fallback the engine printed.
